name: subject-standard-oidc-shape
provenance: Standard OIDC shape, constructed to exercise every subject field at once.

name: subject-permissions-from-permissions-array
provenance: Constructed to exercise the permissions branch of the permissions/scope fallback, with both claims present.

name: subject-permissions-from-scope-fallback
provenance: Constructed to exercise the scope branch of the permissions/scope fallback. `scope` is space-delimited in Keycloak, Auth0 and Cognito alike.

name: subject-teams-from-teams-array
provenance: Constructed to exercise the teams branch of the teams/groups fallback, with both claims present.

name: subject-teams-from-groups-fallback
provenance: Constructed to exercise the groups branch of the teams/groups fallback.

name: subject-string-valued-roles-is-ignored
provenance: Constructed: a string where an array is expected. The shape a configured map is most likely to accept where the Rust mapper does not.

name: subject-string-valued-teams-falls-through-to-groups
provenance: Constructed: an unusable shape on the first candidate must not stop the fallback chain.

name: subject-string-valued-permissions-falls-through-to-scope
provenance: Constructed: the permissions/scope pair with an unusable first candidate.

name: subject-non-string-elements-in-a-role-array-are-skipped
provenance: Constructed: a mixed-type array. Elements that are not strings are dropped, the array as a whole is not rejected.

name: subject-empty-permissions-array-does-not-fall-through-to-scope
provenance: Constructed: an empty array is a usable shape, so it resolves and the chain stops. A configured map that treated empty as unresolved would diverge here.

name: subject-array-valued-scope-contributes-nothing
provenance: Constructed: the Rust mapper reads scope through an as_str accessor, so an array-valued scope contributes nothing. A candidate that accepted the array would grant permissions the mapper does not.

name: subject-an-array-element-containing-whitespace-stays-whole
provenance: Constructed: the shape that separates splitting a delimited string from splitting an array. A field whose candidates are an array and a delimited string must not split the array's elements.

name: subject-a-null-claim-reaches-the-bag-and-maps-nothing
provenance: Constructed: JSON null is present but unusable for a collection field, and is still a policy-visible claim where it was not consumed.

name: subject-missing-anchor-declines
provenance: Constructed: no `sub`, so there is no subject to gate on and the mapper declines.

name: subject-non-string-anchor-declines
provenance: Constructed: `sub` present but not a string, which is a decline rather than a coercion.

name: subject-keycloak-access-token
provenance: Keycloak 26 access token, per the server-admin guide and OIDCLoginProtocolFactory's built-in mappers. Nested realm and per-client roles, space-delimited scope, hyphenated allowed-origins.

name: subject-auth0-user-token-with-a-namespaced-roles-claim
provenance: Auth0 user access token. The roles claim is URL-namespaced because Auth0's restricted-claim list forbids a bare `roles`; `permissions` requires RBAC plus the add-permissions toggle.

name: subject-cognito-id-token
provenance: Cognito ID token, per the Cognito Developer Guide. `cognito:groups` holds group names; `cognito:roles` holds IAM role ARNs, which are not application roles.

name: subject-kubernetes-projected-service-account-token
provenance: Kubernetes projected ServiceAccount token, per the authentication reference. `kubernetes.io` is a top-level claim name containing a dot over a nested object.

name: client-anchor-from-client-id
provenance: Constructed to exercise the client_id branch of the client_id/azp fallback, with both claims present.

name: client-anchor-from-azp
provenance: Constructed to exercise the azp branch of the client_id/azp fallback. Keycloak user flows and Auth0's default profile both send azp rather than client_id.

name: client-a-present-but-unusable-client-id-declines-rather-than-using-azp
provenance: Constructed: the Rust mapper picks the first anchor key that is present and only then requires a string, so a null client_id denies rather than falling through to azp.

name: client-a-numeric-client-id-declines-rather-than-using-azp
provenance: Constructed: the same presence-before-shape rule for a non-null wrong type.

name: client-scopes-from-authorized-scopes
provenance: Constructed to exercise the authorized_scopes branch of the authorized_scopes/scope fallback, with both claims present.

name: client-scopes-from-scope-fallback
provenance: Constructed to exercise the scope branch of the authorized_scopes/scope fallback.

name: client-empty-authorized-scopes-array-does-not-fall-through-to-scope
provenance: Constructed: an empty array is a usable shape, so it resolves and `scope` is never read.

name: client-array-valued-scope-contributes-nothing
provenance: Constructed: the client-side pair of the array-valued scope case.

name: client-an-array-element-containing-whitespace-stays-whole
provenance: Constructed: the client-side pair of the subject case, where order makes the result fully observable.

name: client-aud-as-a-string
provenance: Keycloak serializes a bare string at one audience (StringOrArraySerializer); Auth0 does the same for a pure M2M token.

name: client-aud-as-an-array
provenance: Keycloak serializes an array at two or more audiences; SPIRE and Kubernetes always do.

name: client-aud-absent
provenance: Cognito access tokens carry no aud by default, and an M2M token can never have one.

name: client-non-string-aud-is-ignored
provenance: Constructed: an unusable aud shape produces no audience rather than failing the map.

name: client-roles-from-an-array
provenance: Constructed: platform-native client roles, which are ordered on the client extension.

name: client-string-valued-roles-is-ignored
provenance: Constructed: a string where an array is expected, on a field with no fallback candidate behind it.

name: client-duplicate-role-elements-are-preserved
provenance: Constructed: the client roles field is a Vec, so a repeated element survives. This is what makes the no-deduplication choice observable.

name: client-name-is-carried-when-present
provenance: Constructed: no researched provider mints client_name, so only an operator's custom claim reaches it.

name: client-keycloak-service-account-token
provenance: Keycloak service-account access token, per ClientManager.addServiceAccountProtocolMappersViaScope. Carries client_id, clientHost, clientAddress and a service-account preferred_username.

name: client-auth0-m2m-access-token
provenance: Auth0 default-profile machine-to-machine access token, per the organizations token sample. `sub` is <clientId>@clients and `aud` is a bare string.

name: client-cognito-access-token-without-aud
provenance: Cognito access token, per the Cognito Developer Guide. No azp exists, no aud by default, and a resource-server scope carries a dot and a slash.

name: client-missing-anchor-declines
provenance: Constructed: neither client_id nor azp, so there is no client to gate on.

name: workload-spiffe-id-from-sub
provenance: SPIFFE JWT-SVID standard: `sub` MUST hold the SPIFFE ID.

name: workload-spiffe-id-from-the-spiffe-id-claim-fallback
provenance: Constructed: a provider that surfaces the SPIFFE ID in its own claim rather than in `sub`.

name: workload-non-spiffe-sub-with-a-bogus-spiffe-id-declines
provenance: Constructed: the prefix check applies to every candidate, so a non-SPIFFE sub cannot smuggle in an arbitrary spiffe_id claim.

name: workload-non-spiffe-sub-alone-declines
provenance: Constructed: a perfectly valid user token must not file a non-SPIFFE identity into the workload slot.

name: workload-spire-jwt-svid
provenance: SPIRE JWT-SVID, per credtemplate/builder.go. `aud` is invariantly an array and there is no `iss`, which the JWT-SVID standard does not specify.

name: workload-spiffe-id-with-no-authority-declines
provenance: Constructed: the trust domain is the URI authority and SPIFFE requires it, so a string carrying the scheme alone names no trust boundary. Tightened in this PR; the mapper previously filed it with an empty trust domain.

name: workload-trust-domain-from-a-spiffe-id-with-no-path
provenance: Constructed: the trust domain is the URI authority, which is the whole identifier when there is no path.
